## Release timeout diagnostic retains an approval that already succeeded

At immutable source `beb5286ac676b0cd21f514a8a309165ba031e6de`, [Daily Release run 41636364452, job 126186907864](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-starter/actions/runs/41636364452/job/126186907864) timed out waiting for protected release PR [#185](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-starter/pull/185). The final error told the maintainer to approve a CI run, although the same log records successful automatic approvals:

- Approved workflow run 41724283593; its checks can now report.
- Approved workflow run 41724283022; its checks can now report.
- Approved workflow run 41724282969; its checks can now report.

Fresh read-only observations of those exact runs:
- [41724283022](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-starter/actions/runs/41724283022): completed, conclusion skipped, observed 2026-11-03T22:57:33.697Z.
- [41724282969](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-starter/actions/runs/41724282969): completed, conclusion success, observed 2026-11-03T22:57:33.701Z.
- [41724283593](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-starter/actions/runs/41724283593): queued, conclusion none, observed 2026-11-03T22:57:33.692Z.

## Exact source and isolated reproduction

The [immutable release workflow](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-starter/blob/beb5286ac676b0cd21f514a8a309165ba031e6de/.github/workflows/release.yml#L470-L491) initializes `awaiting_approval=0` once before polling. It sets the flag to `1` after encountering pending runs even if approval succeeds, and never resets it when a subsequent poll has no pending approval. The timeout branch consults that historical flag instead of current unresolved approval state.

An isolated Bash probe extracted the exact timeout branch from the Git-blob-hash-verified workflow. With one simulated successful approval, followed by an empty pending-approval set, it still printed the approval-required instruction and exited 1. No GitHub API, real approval, merge, publication or tag command was executed by the probe. This confirms the diagnostic branch, not the runner scheduling cause or a complete workflow replay.

## Expected, actual and impact

Expected: report currently unresolved approval only. When approved runs are queued/running or checks are otherwise unsettled, explain that current state without asking for a redundant approval.

Actual: an earlier approval requirement permanently selects the approval-required timeout message. This can send maintainers to an already approved run and obscure the actual remaining merge/check state. Fixing this message alone is not evidence the release would merge.

The current run explicitly reported that nothing was published or tagged. Preserve that fail-closed protected-merge/publication behavior. No security bypass, runtime data-loss or successful registry-publication claim is made.

## Source goal and deduplication

The canonical [release record pm-starter-nf9d](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-starter/blob/beb5286ac676b0cd21f514a8a309165ba031e6de/.agents/pm/issues/pm-starter-nf9d.toon) documents distinguishing parked approval from other merge-wait conditions. Its closed delivery does not address the sticky historical flag. Reviewed all 185 issue/PR bodies across all states and 87 canonical PM records. No existing repository-local record was found for this narrow diagnostic defect. The analogous defect is already tracked separately in [pm-ado#84](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/issues/84).

## Acceptance / regression criteria

- Successful approval followed by no currently awaiting runs never produces an approval-needed instruction.
- A current action-required run whose approval failed remains identified with its verified run link.
- Queued/running or failed checks are reported as such, without attributing them to historical approval.
- Test the state transition across polling iterations, not only a permanently true/false flag.
- Timeout continues to refuse publication/tagging before protected merge succeeds.
- Failed approval-state reads remain explicitly unknown; do not silently treat them as an empty set or confirmed approval.
Release timeout asks for workflow approval after automatic approval succeeded
